techniques.evidence: scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:506 The regex half runs on the unmasked body, so a comment can satisfy the guard. chainsGuard and the content rules use source-mask, but this check does not.

scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:484 The tenancy-manifest finding is keyed on whether tenancy.ts was touched at all. Any edit to that file clears it, whether or not the new table was listed.

scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:24 The override channel is a commit trailer that the gated author (about 90% AI per the header) writes inside the same range it authorises. Only `secret` is fenced (UNWAIVABLE_RULES, line 158).

scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:222 The blocking skip rule matches only literal call spellings. Alias, destructure or computed forms (`const t = test; t.skip(`, `test['skip'](`) pass silently, and no escape form is refused.

scripts/review/agent-review.mjs:222 A single model run blocks the required 'Agent review (judgement)' check. The instrument is variable (DEFAULT_MODEL comes from an env override or an alias, with no seed and no all-of-N aggregation), and no pin/assert/aggregate trigger is written beside it.

scripts/review/agent-review.mjs:255 Could-not-run is routed to exit 0 on a required check whose green authorises merging. The keyless path exits 0 too. constitution-check.mjs:718 does this correctly with exit 2.
scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:130 A trailer has to name rule + file[:line] to waive anything. Shapeless or unmatched trailers are reported as waiver-unmatched, and secret is unwaivable.

scripts/review/gate-check.mjs:159 It compares the committed ruleset against the jobs the workflows emit, in both directions (required-but-absent blocks, emitted-but-unrequired is noted), and has an optional live --verify against GitHub. It does not model job-level `if:` skips.
scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:759 The exit code comes from the same blockedBy() the renderer uses, so a blocking finding reaches the exit path.
scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:163 The rendered report and the exit code read one enumeration, so the two surfaces cannot disagree.
scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:13 The same script runs in the pre-push hook and in review.yml (the binding rung).
scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:650 Its green states which question it answered and points to the other lens.
scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:494 The remedy names an in-tree ADR that exists (docs/architecture/decisions/0002-…).
scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:298 The skip-with-reason rule is decided inside a bounded 8-line window of the call, which is a locally decidable property.

scripts/review/agent-review.mjs:75 The two lenses run on different substrates (regex vs model), so the precondition does not hold. The judgement brief does state its negative scope and names who owns it anyway.

pairs.registryProposal: waiver-names-its-finding treats a targeted trailer as sufficient. When the gated party is an agent that writes the commit message in the same range, a perfectly targeted waiver is still a self-reported override (self-reported-gate-inputs). The waiver technique could cross-reference that, saying who may author the trailer and not only what it names.

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: scripts/lint/ruff-ratchet.mjs:250 The ruff ratchet lifts only the config-level ignore list and runs without --ignore-noqa, so inline `# noqa` comments still suppress. pipeline/ carries 118 of them, including 15 F401 and 12 E731 in selected rule families (ruff.toml ignore = [] is empty). None of these are counted, and moving a suppression from the list to an inline comment clears the ratchet.

techniques.evidence: scripts/lint/ruff-ratchet.mjs:250 The ratchet is keyed on WHERE a suppression is written (a lint.ignore entry), not on the property (violations suppressed). That key can be moved to `# noqa` without changing the debt. The TS side counts inline directives, so this asymmetry is Python-only.

scripts/perf/ci-budget.mjs:45 A wall-clock measurement exits 1 on every PR run (its own header line 16 calls it 'a blocking check in CI'). Its written promotion path is to become a required check once the ceilings are measured, but the variance is in the instrument. check-budget.mjs:18 is the conformant counter-example: it uses the static graph, not a stopwatch.
scripts/lint/ts-ratchet.mjs:186 A zero-file walk is fatal (exit 1) and never reads as clean. design:check has a parsed-input floor at check-design-tokens.mjs:103.
scripts/lint/ratchet.mjs:207 The shared ladder maps undeclared/unexplained/grew to BLOCKING, and that reaches the exit code.

scripts/lint/ruff-ratchet.mjs:17 It asks the engine for the resolved violation counts instead of grepping the config, which closes the 'declared rule reports zero' gap. The inline-noqa layer stays open (see renameable-detector-keys).
scripts/lint/ts-ratchet.mjs:39 Precision was measured over the whole population before an `any` counter was built, and the counter was declined.
scripts/lint/ts-ratchet.mjs:42 The `any` question is explicitly assigned to the instrument that owns it.
scripts/lint/ts-ratchet.mjs:22 Ceilings are per rule with a required `why`, so there is no blanket allowance that a new class can hide under.
scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs:13 The prose barrel-import rule was turned into a blocking import-graph budget held by test:perf.
scripts/perf/ci-budget.mjs:101 Unmeasured jobs are skipped and announced. An unreadable run is exit 2 NOT MEASURED, never a pass.
scripts/lint/ruff-ratchet.mjs:263 When ruff cannot run, the message says what is missing and gives an install path the reader can actually use.
scripts/lint/ts-ratchet.mjs:69 The same script runs at the merge rung (ci.yml) and, per AGENTS.md, in pre-push.

pairs.registryProposal: The ratchet guidance (ratchet-design / match-the-resolved-artifact) should name inline suppressions the engine still honours after the config-level ignore is lifted (`# noqa`, without --ignore-noqa) as a standard blind spot. A ratchet that lifts only the list is answering half its own question.
